marker.description: A green-headed pin inserted into the gallbladder.

main_question: Identify the structure indicated by the green pin.
main_explanation: The green pin is inserted into the gallbladder, which is located in the gallbladder fossa on the visceral surface of the liver.

supporting_question.question: Which of the following structures is NOT part of the hepatoduodenal ligament?
supporting_question.explanation: The hepatoduodenal ligament contains the proper hepatic artery, the portal vein, and the common bile duct. The hepatic duct joins the cystic duct to form the common bile duct, so it is not a component of the ligament itself.

true_false.statement: The average volume of the gallbladder is approximately 30-50 ml.
true_false.explanation: The normal capacity of the gallbladder is typically cited as 30 to 50 milliliters.
